impl.summary:
Fixed all six reviewed defects from the door-blast step and all six from the impact-kit step in one commit, e8e581c, on codex/game-presentation in the wt-game worktree. It is not pushed. I checked each defect against the code first, and all 12 were real.

Door blast and junction (verify:blowback-1):
1. Severity 3, blast outcome. `PressureLine.is_in_blast` (360..540) is now the only thing that decides the blast. The blast hurtbox (`blast_hazard`) is removed. If the engineer is in the zone when the fuse ends, they are knocked down and autosave A comes back with the door still sealed. Outside the zone, the door blows and autosave B is written. Physics overlap can no longer contradict this. The 0.4 s hurtbox that used to linger after the blast is gone, because it could only cause a knockdown after B was already written.
2. Severity 2, vent zone. `PressureLine` now has `VENT_GRATE_MIN_X/MAX_X` (264..336). `VENT_MIN_X/MAX_X` (250..350, used for the hint and `is_on_vent`) are the grate plus `M0State.HUMAN_HALF_WIDTH`. The vent hurtbox is exactly the grate and the grate is drawn at that width. Where the vent range touches the breaker range, the vent warning now wins over the breaker hint while the line builds.
3. Severity 2, gauge over the label. The dial now sits above the pipe run at y 266. The stills also showed the door art clipping the end of "SEAL CHARGED" and "VALVE 0 / 3", so the valve label is centred 22 px left of the wheel.
4. Severity 1, crafted save. v4 junction saves with `door_blown` false are rejected if either actor's body would reach past the door face (`M0State.JUNCTION_DOOR_LEFT_X` 452, half-widths 14 and 31).
5. Severity 1, labels after the blast. Once the door is down, the breaker and valve read BREAKER SPENT / VALVE SPENT, the breaker light dims, all three turn lights stay green and the wheel rests at three quarters. This is the same right after the blast and after Continue.
6. Severity 1, hidden knockdown. A knocked-down engineer draws at z 3, above WOLF at z 2, and goes back to 2 on restore or cancel. The vent burst is now alpha 0.3 with 16 particles spread over the grate.

I also picked up one of the open issues from implement:blowback-1. With Reduced Motion on, the charged door seam glows steadily instead of strobing. The Settings toggle now reaches the junction room.

Impact kit (verify:foundation):
- **Changelog overclaim:** the October 8 bullet now says only the gate and the Records exit flash the screen.
- **Hazard comment and mask:** the comment now describes how Area2D detection actually works. The hazard's collision layer is 0, and the Human `collision_mask` is back to 2, as on main.
- **Rumble device:** `Impact.rumble_device` is set from the device of the last joypad input instead of always being 0.
- **Sound budget:** the test bound is now 100 ms, with a comment explaining the slack for CI.
- **Bank switch-off:** setting `SfxBank.enabled` to false now stops everything playing, loops included.
- **Restore line:** it says "Back at the start of this beat." when restoring from the in-memory snapshot, and "Back at the last autosave." only when restoring from disk.

Tests added:
- **junction_test, blast edge:** at x 352 the door blows with no knockdown, the line says "The seal goes" and B is written. At x 362 it is a knockdown and the door stays sealed.
- **junction_test, vent edges:** at x 242 a vent trip gives no knockdown and no vent hint. At x 256 the hint warns and the trip knocks the engineer down, with the engineer drawn above WOLF and a translucent burst, then autosave A is restored.
- **junction_test, geometry:** the hurtbox equals the grate, and the constants match the scene's body and door widths.
- **junction_test, labels and Reduced Motion:** SPENT labels after the blast and after Continue; the seam is steady with Reduced Motion and strobes without it.
- **junction_test, saves:** v4 accepts actors pressed against the door (438 / 421), rejects 439, 600 and WOLF at 700, and accepts both actors past the door once it is blown.
- **impact_test:** rumble follows device 1 and then device 0, and the snapshot restore line.
- **sfx_bank_test:** switching the bank off stops a loop and a one-shot that are already playing.

Docs: added a new "## October 9, 2026" section with seven spoiler-free bullets, corrected the October 8 flash bullet, updated service-junction.mdx and the Reduced Motion row in settings.mdx, and regenerated changelog.txt with export_changelog.py. No asset files changed, so manifest.json is untouched.

impl.summary:
Beats 4-6 of Blowback are built and committed as 27a4a4c on codex/game-presentation, in the worktree only. It is not pushed. Nobody has played it yet, so feel, pacing, readability and audio quality are not validated.

New files:
- **SentryBrain** (scripts/sentry_brain.gd) is pure logic. Its `tick(delta, engineer_x, engineer_exposed, bait_x)` returns patrol, chase, fixated or down. It also has a dormant state before the blast wakes it.
  - Patrol runs 600..840 at 140 px/s; chase runs at 230 px/s. It sees the engineer only in its lane, ahead of it (180 px) or touching. The ARM PANEL alcove (556..584) hides the engineer.
  - It stops 41 px past the lane edge, so an engineer back over the rubble can never be touched. It gives up 2.5 s after the engineer is back over the rubble.
  - When WOLF draws it, it parks 40 px short of him, which puts it on the floor mark at 700.
  - It does not tick while waiting for a choice (its paused flag), while the game is paused, or during a knockdown.
- **Sentry** (scripts/sentry.gd) is a CharacterBody2D that moves the same way M0Actor does. It is on no physics layer and scans none, so it never blocks the actors. All its drawing is in one `Visual` child: a provisional code-drawn tracked machine whose eye strip shows its state.
- **DropArm** (scripts/drop_arm.gd): 0.45 s fall; a hit when |sentry_x − 700| ≤ 44; a miss starts a 6 s rewind before it can drop again and a 3 s coolant cloud with its own hurtbox.

Changes to existing files:
- **M0State** gains `drop_sentry()`, `clear_junction()` and `wolf_will_bait()`. The last uses the same rule as the relay contact.
- **JunctionRoom** now draws the arm, cable, tank, floor-mark stripes (exactly the hit window), the alcove, the exit bolt box and a sliding hatch.
- **main.gd** adds the rubble-line question at `JunctionRoom.CHOICE_X`:
  - Answer 1 with the DISCLOSE memory: WOLF chooses to draw the sentry from `WOLF_BAIT_X`.
  - Answer 1 with the PRESS memory: WOLF refuses with a line that carries no blame.
  - Answer 2: the engineer times the drop alone.
- **Tank hit** (BOOM 2): hit-stop, flash, shake, rumble, boom, coolant and sparks; `sentry_down` is set and autosave C is written.
- **Tank miss**: dull clang, the cloud, the sentry chases the panel, and WOLF breaks off if he was drawing it.
- **Exit bolt**: 0.6 s whine, then the arc (flash, shake 0.8, sparks, clank) and the hatch opens. Using the hatch writes autosave D and plays a short closing beat; Continue there returns to the title.
- **Knockdowns**: sentry contact and the coolant cloud both restore autosave B.
- **Pause, Back and focus-loss**: the new question and the closing beat use the existing pause path. No new input actions.
- **SfxBank** gets three new generated clips: a servo loop, a winch loop and the bolt whine.

Fixes made after looking at the stills:
- The tank now hangs at y 300 instead of 250, so the on-screen answers no longer cover it.
- The cloud is fainter and drawn behind the actors so it no longer hides the sentry.
- WOLF's hold spot at the rubble moved to 448 so he no longer covers the engineer.
- The sentry is drawn larger (half-width 26).
- The hint during a chase now says to get back over the rubble.
- The closing camera stays inside the room.

Docs, the changelog and the asset register are updated:
- The Service Junction walkthrough has new sections 4-6.
- Spoiler-free bullets went under the existing October 9 heading, and `apps/game/assets/changelog.txt` was regenerated.
- The manifest's sound-effect entry and status line cover the new clips and the code-drawn sentry.

Things that differ from the spec:
- The hit is judged where the tank lands, not when you tap. On the engineer-only route you have to tap about 63 px early to allow for the fall; the hint says the tank takes a moment to fall.
- New sounds play without stereo panning (the spec asked for positional players).
- The lights-out aftermath (the planned cut line) is skipped; WOLF's refusal line is kept.

defects.title: Sentry's patrol turn drives into the engineer hidden in the ARM PANEL alcove
defects.location: apps/game/scripts/sentry_brain.gd:10 (PATROL_MIN_X 600) with :24 (HALF_WIDTH 26); apps/game/scripts/junction_room.gd ARM_X 570 / _draw_arm_panel
defects.detail: At the left patrol turn the sentry's centre is x 600, so its body's left edge is at 574. An engineer standing at the panel (ARM_X 570, body 556..584) overlaps it by 10 px, and the drawn alcove (542..598) by 24 px. is_exposed() is false in the alcove, so nothing happens. The engineer (z 2) draws in front of the machine (z 1), so on every pass the sentry visibly runs into the 'hidden' engineer without consequence. The docs say 'touching it is a knockdown', so this contradicts them and muddies the one contact rule the lane teaches. Reproduced in evidence/blowback2/review-probe/01-alcove-bounce.png (brain_x 602.9, human_x 570, fail false). Fix it without moving the approved hit window: turn the patrol at the body's front edge (centre >= COVER_MAX_X + HUMAN_HALF_WIDTH + HALF_WIDTH, about 624; 624..840 still crosses the mark at 700), or narrow the drawn body. Then re-check the alcove-safety test and recapture.

defects.title: Patrol resumes after a chase with a 30 px jump of the brain's position
defects.location: apps/game/scripts/sentry_brain.gd:127-136 (_patrol reflection)
defects.detail: A chase parks the brain at CHASE_MIN_X (586), below PATROL_MIN_X, still facing left. The engineer is already behind the rubble then, so it is harmless today. Fix: when patrol starts outside 600..840, face into the range and walk back at PATROL_SPEED instead of reflecting.

defects.title: Sentry servo and winch play non-positional sound
defects.location: apps/game/scripts/main.gd:1489 (_lane_sound) via SfxBank loop AudioStreamPlayer
defects.detail: The spec's Audio section says 'Vent, sentry and tank use AudioStreamPlayer2D for panning'. I checked all four reviewer defects against the code. Three were real and are fixed in one commit, 998f575 on codex/game-presentation (not pushed). The fourth is a deviation from the audio spec that was already there before this step, so I left it for the audio pass.

defects.title: A spent breaker re-arms after any reload with the door already blown, which allows a phantom blast and a knockdown
defects.location: apps/game/scripts/main.gd:1799 (_sync_junction_room: pressure_line.reset() always returns the line to idle) together with main.gd:1264 (_interact_junction tries pressure_line.arm() before the door_blown 'spent' branch) and main.gd:1640-1646 (_door_blast runs _blast_feedback and the PressureLine.is_in_blast knockdown before checking state.blow_door())
defects.detail: After the door blows, the live line sits in 'blown' and arm() refuses. Every _sync_scene resets it to idle: Continue at autosave B, C or D, and every sentry or cloud knockdown that restores B. Pressing USE at the breaker then arms it again even though the labels read BREAKER SPENT / VALVE SPENT. The hiss plays, vent steam emits, touch USE becomes CRANK, and the valve takes turns again. The relief vent can trip and knock the engineer down. A charged seal lights the fuse, and when it ends _door_blast plays the boom, flash, shake and rumble for a door that is already gone. If the engineer is anywhere in x 360..540, which includes the rubble line at CHOICE_X 526, the result is a BLAST_REASON knockdown. With the door unblown, the valve hint also reads 'The valve is dead. Arm the breaker' instead of spent. I reproduced this headless in a scratch copy: a v4 save with door_blown, then Continue, then USE at x 200 gave line=building and the status 'The overload breaker catches'. Cranking at x 410 reached fuse, and the engineer was knocked down with 'The door blew with you in front of it'. No test covers USE at the breaker after Continue at B. This breaks the rules that feedback comes from real state changes and that a spent machine is not a hazard. Fix: in _sync_junction_room set the line to blown, or a spent state, when state.door_blown is true, or check state.door_blown before pressure_line.arm() and before the valve/hold path. Also make _door_blast return before any feedback when the door is already blown.

defects.title: If the save file can't be read, a junction knockdown falls back to a stale corridor beat snapshot
defects.location: apps/game/scripts/main.gd:1702-1722 (_restore_beat) with _mark_beat only called in the corridor (finish intro, choice, breaker, relay)
defects.detail: _restore_beat loads from disk when state.checkpoint_reached is true and load_from_disk succeeds. Otherwise it uses beat_snapshot. Only corridor beats write that snapshot. _enter_junction, the junction autosaves and _load_game never refresh or clear it. If the checkpoint file goes missing or becomes unreadable mid-session (deleted or corrupted externally), a vent, blast, sentry or cloud knockdown restores the lockdown-chapter snapshot. That snapshot can even come from an earlier New Game in the same session. It throws the engineer back several chapters, which breaks 'loses at most the current beat'. This only happens after a disk failure, so the severity is low. Fix: clear beat_snapshot in _load_game and _enter_junction, or call _mark_beat at each junction autosave, so the fallback is never older than the current beat.

Estimated per-frame fill in play: base rect 1.0 + far plate 1.0 + haze about 0.6 + mid plate 1.0 (a full-screen alpha quad) + post_grade multiply 1.0 + near strips about 0.2 + glows, shafts and dust. That should be fine on mid-range GPUs but is marginal on low-end Mali/PowerVR at 60 fps. Dropping the base rect, or drawing it only when the far plate is missing, removes about 20% of that fill. Not measured on a device.

defects.title: Hit-stop replacement test races a 90 ms real-time timer with a 65 ms check
defects.location: apps/game/tests/impact_test.gd:64-67
defects.detail: hit_stop(0.05) followed by hit_stop(0.09) starts a 90 ms real-time restore timer. The test then waits 65 ms of real time and expects time_scale to still be 0.05. Both SceneTreeTimers ignore time scale and are checked once per frame, and the restore timer was created first. So if any frame stalls past about 25 ms (a loaded CI runner, GC, or the sequential import before it), both fire in the same frame, time_scale is already back to 1.0, and the check fails even though the code is correct. Widening the gap (for example hit_stop(0.02) then hit_stop(0.1) with a check at 0.04) or checking _stop_serial instead of wall-clock time would make it deterministic.

defects.title: Sound-bank budget assertion is wall-clock based, with a margin under 3x
defects.location: apps/game/tests/sfx_bank_test.gd:26-28; apps/game/scripts/sfx_bank.gd:47-48 (generate() in _ready, built from main.gd:341-343)
defects.detail: The test fails if generation takes 100 ms or more. On this machine three runs took 37.5, 37.7 and 39.2 ms, not the 16 ms the comment claims, so a slower or busier runner can fail the gate without any code change. At runtime the same work, about 146k GDScript per-sample iterations plus 146k encode_s16 calls, runs synchronously in Main._ready before the first frame. Scaled from 38 ms, that is an estimated 150 to 300 ms on a low-end phone's GDScript VM (estimate only). That is a one-time boot cost rather than an in-play stall. Possible fixes: generate lazily or on a WorkerThreadPool task, or bake the deterministic buffers at export. The test should check determinism and length rather than time, or use a much looser bound.

finalFix.summary:
I checked all 14 reported defects against the code. 13 were real and are fixed in four commits on codex/game-presentation (8f6fb36, d4fe540, 81b72d6, 567b362). The sound-bank defect is only partly fixed: its test is fixed, but the sound bank still builds its sounds while the game starts. Nothing was pushed.

1. Spent breaker re-arming after a reload (defects 1 and 3, the same bug): PressureLine.reset(spent) now restores a blown door's line as blown, not idle. _interact_junction checks state.door_blown before arm() and before the valve. _hold_station returns nothing once the door is down. _door_blast returns before any sound or flash if the door is already down. Standing on the vent after the blast now gives the normal "no station" line instead of the vent warning. The test now loads autosave B and uses the breaker and valve: the line stays blown, no turns are taken, a stray blast does nothing and nothing is saved.

2. Old fallback snapshot and the "use a station" retry (defects 2 and 4): every autosave now refreshes the fallback snapshot, even when the write fails, and Continue (_load_game) refreshes it too. New Game clears it. A new save_pending flag makes a knockdown restore the step that failed to save instead of the older file on disk. The next USE anywhere in the room retries the write, so the existing "Save failed. Use a station to try again." hint is now true and its text is unchanged. Tests cover a failed autosave B while an older autosave A is on disk, the retry on USE, and a save file that can't be read.

3. Camera pan on room entry: entering Records Access or the Service Junction now cuts the camera to the engineer. Covered by a test and a still.

4. Touch buttons hiding legs and props: the gameplay zoom stays 1.35. With the arrows and USE on screen, the camera sits lower (y 392 instead of 360), so feet and machine bases land at screen y 335, above the buttons (which start at y 345). It goes back to y 360 while answer buttons show, so the hanging tank stays visible below them. The cost: the ceiling lamps leave the top of the view on touch. Tests check the feet against the buttons and the background coverage at the new framing.

5. Junction pipes through captions: the breaker pipe now has a gap behind the OVERLOAD BREAKER label. The vent pipe runs down to a nozzle above its floor grate. The RELIEF VENT caption now sits just above the grate, in the theme font. The first spot I tried put it under the right edge of the junction's closing shot and failed the sentry test, so I moved it.

6. Texture memory: the six room plates are now imported VRAM-compressed (S3TC on desktop, ETC2 on mobile). The two near plates are cropped to the 512x1080 strip the game draws, with pixels unchanged; the originals are in commit 9a52666. The full-screen base fill under the far plate is only drawn when a room has no far plate. Side-by-side crops of the desktop stills show no visible banding. Mobile ETC2 quality and the memory and load-time gains were not checked on a device.

7. Flaky timing tests: the hit-stop test now fires the shorter timeout by hand, with no timer race. The sound-bank timing limit went from 100 ms to 400 ms; length and determinism checks are the real gate.

8. Wording: the manifest now lists the Service Junction for the WOLF and Rowan sprites, describes the purge display as wall-mounted with no label or reflection, and records the near-plate crop and VRAM import. The docs now say Reduced Motion skips the fall in a knockdown (first steps and settings pages). The saves, troubleshooting and input pages describe the save retry and the touch camera. Six spoiler-free bullets went under the existing October 9 heading, which was already in place, and changelog.txt was regenerated.
